intro: A depthwise separable convolution first filters each channel independently, then mixes channels at each location. That factorization restricts the filters a layer can represent.
task: Implement valid spatial cross-correlation per channel followed by a pointwise linear mixture. Trace the two stages on inputs whose channels have very different magnitudes.
requirements: images has nonempty shape (B,C,H,W). depthwise_weights has shape (C,Kh,Kw), with 1<=Kh<=H and 1<=Kw<=W. pointwise_weights has shape (O,C), with O>0.
Use stride one, no padding and no bias. For each channel, sum image[b,c,y+u,x+v]*depthwise_weights[c,u,v] over the kernel axes without flipping the kernel.
Mix the filtered channels with pointwise_weights: output[b,o,y,x]=sum_c pointwise_weights[o,c]*filtered[b,c,y,x]. Return shape (B,O,H-Kh+1,W-Kw+1).
Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, in addition to the bounds above. Leave all inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Do not flip the spatial kernel

hints.title: Keep channels separate during spatial filtering
hints.body: The first stage does not sum across the input channel axis.

hints.title: Mix only after filtering
hints.body: Each pointwise output channel is a weighted sum of the filtered input channels at the same spatial position.

explanation: The equivalent dense kernel is W[o,c,u,v]=pointwise_weights[o,c]*depthwise_weights[c,u,v]. For a given input channel, every output uses a scaled version of the same spatial filter.
This factorization uses C*Kh*Kw+O*C weights instead of O*C*Kh*Kw. It changes expressiveness as well as parameter count; arbitrary dense kernels need not factor this way.
Adapted the upstream depthwise and pointwise operations to NumPy with explicit spatial slices. Removed singleton weight axes and retained valid stride-one cross-correlation semantics.
